events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Abandoned Supplies

options.text: Grab their weapons and armor.
Take any food they left behind.

events.text: You have come across an abandoned enemy supply cache after your recent victory, but your troops can only carry so much. What should they take?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Among the Dead

options.text: These things happen in wartime.

events.text: Following the heated battle, General [character] walks the battlefield. He discovers a familiar figure among the dead: [character], the heir of [rival]. It is too late to keep this tragic news a secret...

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Barracks Heir

options.text: Accept their demands.
Refuse to treat with this mutinous force.
Ask that they trust your strength to chose an heir.

events.text: Loyalty is a fickle thing. After a string of wins led by [character], the troops are becoming increasingly bound to him. It reaches a peak when, after another victory, an officer places the symbolic vestments of royalty on [character] and proclaims him the true heir of [rival]. Emboldened by support throughout the military, a message shortly arrives not so gently stating that [character]’s forces recognize him as the heir to [rival] and that they expect you to do the same. Shall we give in to this demand?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Battlefield Promotion

options.text: Grant the [unit] extra experience.
Hold a celebration in [city]!
We cannot afford such extravagance.

events.text: Under the brave leadership of General [character], our [unit] has shown exemplary courage on the battlefield. How shall our [unit] be recognized?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Be Victorious in This

options.text: Accept [character] tale.
Encourage [character] to find strength from this new God.
Stop this [religion] nonsense.

events.text: [character] has led his troops to a resounding victory over the [rival] forces. The General claims to have been granted a vision on the way to the fight, in which a flaming cross appeared in the sky, with the words "Through this sign will you conquer." Under [character] instructions, his [unit] daubed the symbol on their shields and armor before the battle. News of this divine victory is quickly spreading through [rival].

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Birth of a Legend

options.text: My scribes shall carve the tales of my exploits on the walls of the palace to inspire all.

events.text: Having won the first of what will surely be many great victories, stories of your prowess in battle begin circulating throughout your Realm.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Brave Deeds

options.text: Publicly praise [character] for his courage.
Commission a poem to celebrate the duel.
Urge [character] to be more careful.

events.text: Rumors reach the court that your heir, [character], was forced into a duel against a towering mercenary champion. Thank the gods, he was victorious! Witnesses claim that [character] dominated his much larger opponent in close combat. How shall we respond?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Captured Noble

options.text: Ransom the prisoner.
Execute him and send the head as a message.
Keep him as a hostage.

events.text: After a victorious battle, [character] chases down a fleeing [rival] noble and takes him prisoner. Such a captive is a rare prize, indeed.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Captured Prisoners

options.text: Ransom them back to their families.
Execute them to send a message.
Resettle them in our cities.

events.text: You captured a number of enemy soldiers in the last skirmish. They are exhausted and demoralized, and many have been grievously wounded. What shall we do with them?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Captured Supplies

options.text: A general mix of weapons and supplies.
Shields to protect against enemy arrows.

events.text: Troops commanded by [character] have successfully executed a daring maneuver to split the enemy forces into small pockets and defeat them. The victory was so swift and decisive that the men captured crates of intact supplies that the enemy never had time to use. Your soldiers are well equipped as it is but can carry some of the captured supplies with them. What should they take to fare best in future battles?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Enemy General Killed

options.text: Invite the officer to your court.
We will honor the fallen.
Praise the soldiers for their success.

events.text: The silence after a battle hangs heavy in the air. Exhausted men sit slumped next to the bodies of the fallen. Cutting through the quiet, a victory cry rings out across the battlefield. A group of soldiers carry the body of the enemy general up to [character], their officer claiming to have cut down the general as he fled.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Famous Victor

options.text: He has earned a reward.
Let's not overdo it.

events.text: Stories of [character]'s bravery in battle spread across the nation like seeds waiting to bear fruit. His name is quickly becoming synonymous with selfless heroism.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Feats of Valor

options.text: Promote him on the battlefield.
Make him an advisor in my court.
Return him to the front lines.

events.text: News from the recent [rival] wars reaches the court. It seems your son [character] distinguished himself valiantly in battle. He is returning to the capital for a parade. How else may we recognize [character]'s service?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Honor and Glory

options.text: Hold military celebrations in his honor.
Revels and feasting in [city] for a week!
Their glory is simply a reflection of my own.

events.text: Stories from the recent battle describe the bravery and leadership of [character], whose troops brought us this victory! How shall we celebrate him?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Inaccurate Troops

options.text: Make them hunt for their own suppers.
Drill them relentlessly until they improve.

events.text: You grow increasingly frustrated with your soldiers' terrible aim. Their mistakes are costing lives. How shall we fix it?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Insolent General

options.text: Hold a celebration in [city] in honor of [character].
My generals serve me. [character] doesn't get to make demands.

events.text: The [family] General [character] has led your forces to victory. He is said to be overjoyed at the victory and to deeply wish for public recognition. Indeed, a message soon follows that all but demands it. As insolent as his behavior is, given our difficult relationship with the [family], honoring [character] could be politically advantageous.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Professional and Proficient

options.text: [character] can conduct additional field training to refine those ideas.
We should apply those ideas when training recruits in [city].

events.text: Having won another victory for [rival], General [character] remarks that leading an army of professional soldiers is very different from the conscript armies he's familiar with through his studies of military history. Professional soldiers do not just differ in pay, they can use different tactics on the battlefield, and should be led differently, [character] concludes.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Proud Demeanor

options.text: [character] did naught but follow my orders. The celebration shall be of my victory.
[character] performed, I suppose, admirably. It is not as if the world shall forget my works, is it?

events.text: [character] broaches the topic carefully. "My [title], you have so many accolades for your many accomplishments... might it not only add to your majesty to grant [character] some measure of glory for this most recent military victory?"

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Rising Star

options.text: Effective units should stay together.
We need more military minds in court.

events.text: After the successful defeat of [rival] forces, General [character] describes the brave feats of one particular soldier, one he believes would make an exemplary court advisor. Should we elevate this natural leader, or is his wisdom better employed on the battlefield?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Ruthless Slaughter

options.text: Let this victory by [character] be the last battle of the war.
This is what we needed to press on against [rival].
We can have honor even in war. My troops will not act like barbarians.

events.text: Troops led by General [character] have prevailed in battle, but the scene was a horrible one. As [rival] soldiers were routed and retreating in disarray, [character] led a charge to kill the panicking enemy. He was seen personally executing a group of [rival] that tried to surrender. Tales of this brutal slaughter have reached [rival] through one of the few survivors, and the [rival] are so discouraged by this display of the savagery of war that they're willing to commit to an immediate truce.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Sword of the Fallen

options.text: It is not my place to accept such a gift.
I will bear the sword proudly.
That sword is cursed, and I will not take it.

events.text: The last [rival] falls beneath a storm of blows, and the skirmish ends at last. Our soldiers cross the battlefield, giving mercy to the wounded and collecting the spoils of war. Among the riches gleaned from the [rival] dead is an ancient, ornate sword, pried from the hands of a dead soldier. The blade is presented to you as a symbol of our glorious victory.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Test of Metal

options.text: I know my strengths. It is my Generals who are really winning this war.
My people now know they have a [title] who will fight for them when needed.
This feels right. I will lead [rival] to victory on the field of battle.

events.text: It is well known that you are not a natural military leader, preferring to <p.is_sub.S1=SUBJECT_SCHOLAR>spend your time reading your scrolls<p=SUBJECT_JUDGE>resolve conflict with your well-honed judgments<else>use less scrupulous means to win your battles<end>. However, [rival] has been faring admirably against [rival] under your guidance, and leading your troops is starting to feel familiar. As you survey the field of your victory and feel the weight of your weapon you feel different. Is this the role you were meant for?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Court's Men

options.text: Deadlier shots.
Greater range.
Ignore distance.
They are worthy of every promotion.

events.text: A group of veteran [unit] has emerged from battle, bloodied but victorious. They attribute their success to the shipments of bodkin arrows recently delivered to their camp. This unit is eager to continue the fight, wishing to honor the court with its kills. For what purpose shall we train these skilled soldiers?

events.author: Solver
events.name: The Fluffy Bunny

tip: As leader: +5% Unit Trait Modifier / Melee
As general: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Melee

options.text: Looks are deceiving - the bunny is very brave if it is here.
It is certainly afraid, but even an animal can overcome its fear with discipline.
Fluffy or not, the bunny will surely not hesitate to feast on the corpses.
This must be a sign from the heavens! We must celebrate our victory with our [religion] citizens.

events.text: As the deafening noise of the battle turns into silence only broken by the moans of the wounded, [character] spots something most unexpected - a fluffy bunny skipping across the battlefield, seemingly not scared by the carnage and the fallen [rival] soldiers. The bunny's endearing looks are so incongruous with the battlefield that [character] is almost as shocked by the fluffster's presence as by the battle that just ended. Just how is he supposed to understand it?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: The People's General
events.text: Victory in battle has increased the fame of the renowned [character]. He has become the subject of popular songs and stories, and our advisors fret over his growing popularity which might yet prove to be a threat to your rule.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Victory for the King

options.text: The victory is a testament to the army's trust in [character].
The troops serve [character] well, just as he serves me well.

events.text: After the victory, [character] holds a speech for his soldiers, dedicating the victory to you, [character]. It takes a brave soldier to fight, he says, and a dedicated general to lead, but it is only with a wise leader that a nation's battles bring prosperity and a brighter future.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Victory for the King

options.text: Gold can buy success on the battlefield. Let's spend some more of it.
The victory is a testament to the army's trust in [character].
The troops serve [character] well, just as he serves me well.

events.text: After the victory, [character] holds a speech for his soldiers, dedicating the victory to you, [character]. It takes a brave soldier to fight, he says, and a dedicated general to lead, but it is only with a wise leader that a nation's battles bring prosperity and a brighter future.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Warrior of [rival]

options.text: Such a bargaining chip could prove useful.
We take no prisoners.

events.text: Among the defeated force, you spot a wounded officer of noble birth.
